what: A solid-color curtain covers the screen and a rounded-box hole opens in its center to reveal the page (.5s expo.in — slow at first, snaps open at the end). Clicking a same-origin link picks one of a few colors at random, and the hole, larger than the screen, shrinks to .475 times the screen size (.65s expo.inOut — only the four corners are covered, rounded) then closes in .4s expo.in, waits .65s and goes to the next page. The next page opens again from the same color curtain. The hole follows the screen ratio, shrinking width and height together, and the corner radius is half the hole width on landscape screens and equal to the width on portrait screens.

options.open: Opening duration in seconds, default .5 — 0 shows it right away with no veil
options.hold: Wait after closing before moving on (seconds), default .25 (the original moves on .65+.65s after shrinking begins)
options.colors: Comma-separated variable names to pick as curtain colors, default --kf-accent,--kf-accent-soft,--kf-ink — the first curtain to open is --kf-ink
options.[data-fx-part=plain]: This link (or links inside it) passes straight through with no block
options.fx:curtain-open: Event the element emits when the curtain is fully open — raise the headline and title then

note: The original draws the curtain with a WebGL shader (screen-width-unit rounded-box distance field + derivative antialiasing) and, being a single-page app, swaps content while the curtain stays closed. Our part draws the same box, radius ratio and curve on a 2D canvas (fill all − erase rounded box) with real page navigation, and passes the chosen color via sessionStorage. Hash links, new windows and other origins are left untouched

from.where: All pages — WebGL rounded box curtain (open 0→1 .5s expo.in · close 1→.475 .65s expo.inOut → 0 .4s expo.in, random pick from an eight-color palette)
